text: HRV-trend rule kept as written (athlete, 2026-11-24, after an evidence check: 7-day lnRMSSD vs 60-day baseline +/- 0.5 SD is the mainstream method; the 0.5 SD width is a convention; Yellow costs little because strength stays). Each weekly review counts the days the HRV trend changed a session and what each change cost. If HRV-driven changes hit more than ~1/3 of training days over 2 weeks, or the trend stays below band 10+ days, the review asks why (sleep, stress, fuel, load, session RPE at the same loads) before changing the plan; any response (early deload, more food, sleep focus) is a proposal. Thresholds are a practitioner heuristic, not evidence. W48 count so far: 2 HRV Yellow days (11-23, 11-24), 1 session change (11-24 AMRAP -> Zone 2 bike).
